findings.pdf_says:
15.8.2   General format

  FUNCTION  ACOS  ( argument-1 )      [FUNCTION and ACOS are both UNDERLINED in the printed general format]
findings.why_it_matters: Underlining in a general format is normative notation (5.2.6): an underlined word is a REQUIRED word. The transcription drops the underline on both FUNCTION and ACOS and wraps the format in a fenced code block instead. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 34068. The house convention everywhere else in clause 15 is `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>NAME</u>` (e.g. ABS line 34026, ANNUITY line 34102, ATAN line 34190), so any tool or reader deriving required-vs-optional words from the markup reads FUNCTION/ACOS as non-required here while reading them as required three formats away.
findings.suggested_repair: Replace the fenced block at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:34066-34069 with `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>ACOS</u> ( argument-1 )` to match the ABS/ANNUITY/ATAN convention on the surrounding pages.

findings.pdf_says:
15.10.2   General format

  FUNCTION  ASIN  ( argument-1 )      [FUNCTION and ASIN are both UNDERLINED in the printed general format]
findings.why_it_matters: Underlining in a general format is normative notation (5.2.6): an underlined word is a REQUIRED word. The transcription drops the underline on both FUNCTION and ASIN and renders the format as inline code. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 34152. Adjacent formats in the same clause do preserve it (`<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>ATAN</u>` at line 34190), so the required-word marking is inconsistent within a two-page span.

findings.pdf_says:
15.12.2   General format

  FUNCTION  BASECONVERT  ( argument-1  argument-2  argument-3 )      [FUNCTION and BASECONVERT are both UNDERLINED in the printed general format]
findings.markdown_says:
### 15.12.2 General format

FUNCTION BASECONVERT ( argument-1 argument-2 argument-3 )
findings.why_it_matters: Underlining in a general format is normative notation (5.2.6): an underlined word is a REQUIRED word. The transcription emits the format as bare prose with no underline markup at all. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 34228. BASECONVERT is a COBOL-2023 addition, so this is precisely the kind of format an implementer reads fresh; losing the required-word marking removes the only signal distinguishing required words from optional keywords.
findings.suggested_repair: Replace specs/ISO_COBOL.md:34228 with `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>BASECONVERT</u> ( argument-1 argument-2 argument-3 )`.
